title: Your starting point
body:
This chapter explains why a service exists, introduces the main areas of study, and outlines the Foundation exam format.

A fictional workplace-support service illustrates the concepts. Later chapters develop the terminology and methods in detail.
note: Original instructional objectives. This pilot alone does not cover the full Foundation syllabus.

title: Digital service work is connected
body:
A useful service depends on people working together throughout its life.

A new feature can change support demand. A recurring incident can reveal a design problem. A supplier decision can affect customer experience.
note: Original conceptual illustration, not an official ITIL figure. The pictured activities are an interpretation for teaching, not a prescribed sequence.

note: Foundation topic overview, paraphrased from PeopleCert. Use the current licensed syllabus for criterion-level coverage. This is an orientation map, not an exhaustive assessment checklist.

title: A workplace example
body:
Contoso employees lose time chasing access to the tools they need. The support team closes many tickets, but new starters still wait.

A useful outcome would be that each new starter can work on the agreed start date. A ticket count alone cannot establish that outcome.
note: Original fictional worked example, not an official exam question.

title: Four perspectives on the same problem
body:
People: clear ownership and appropriate training.
Technology: consistent information across connected systems.
Partners: coordinated responsibilities with external suppliers.
Work: visible handoffs, waiting time and repeated activity.
note: Original teaching interpretation of the four dimensions. Formal dimension names: Organizations and People; Information and Technology; Partners and Suppliers; Value Streams and Processes.

title: The Foundation exam
body:
40 multiple-choice questions
60 minutes
Closed book
65% minimum pass mark
note: Source: PeopleCert ITIL Foundation (Version 5) certification page, checked 15 November 2026 (SGT). 65% of 40 is 26. Confirm current booking conditions before the exam.

title: Understanding the exam format
body:
The Foundation assessment uses multiple-choice questions and is closed book.

The published duration is 60 minutes for 40 questions. A 65% pass mark corresponds to 26 correct answers out of 40.
note: Exam facts from the PeopleCert Foundation (Version 5) certification page. The 26-answer threshold is calculated from the published pass percentage and question count. This slide explains logistics; it contains no practice examination.

title: A concept-focused reading approach
body:
Read each concept in the licensed learning material.
Connect the terminology to its purpose and intended outcome.
Use the Contoso example to see the idea in context.
Summarise the relationships in plain language.
Revisit unclear terms using the official glossary.
note: Original reading guidance. This pilot includes no practice examinations, videos or hands-on labs.

title: Worked example: activity versus outcome
body:
Contoso closes 30% more tickets, but new starters still wait three days for access. More activity does not necessarily mean better outcomes.

A useful measure is the share of starters with working access by their agreed start time. Reviewing approval queues can reveal the delay.
note: Original fictional worked example. Ticket volume measures activity; timely usable access reflects the intended outcome. Reviewing waiting time at approval handoffs helps locate a possible improvement opportunity. No learner task or lab is required.
